questions.title: Group Anagrams
questions.description:
Read a single line of space-separated lowercase words from stdin. Group the words so that any two words that are anagrams of each other (they use exactly the same letters, with the same multiplicity, just possibly in a different order) fall into the same group.

### Input
A single line containing space-separated lowercase words.
```
eat tea tan ate nat bat
```

### Output
Print one group per line, each group's words separated by single spaces, following these rules exactly:

1. **Within each group**, sort the words alphabetically ascending.
2. **Order the groups** by comparing each group's (already-sorted) first word, alphabetically ascending.
3. **Duplicate words are kept.** If the same word appears twice in the input, it appears twice within its group — it is not de-duplicated.

### Example
Input:
```
eat tea tan ate nat bat
```
Output:
```
ate eat tea
bat
nat tan
```
`eat`, `tea`, `ate` are anagrams of each other, sorted alphabetically to `ate eat tea`. `tan`, `nat` are anagrams, sorted to `nat tan`. `bat` is alone in its group. The three groups are then ordered by their first word: `ate` < `bat` < `nat`.

testCases.description: normal mixed case: several anagram groups plus a singleton
testCases.input: eat tea tan ate nat bat
testCases.expectedOutput:
ate eat tea
bat
nat tan

testCases.description: all words are anagrams of each other -> one group
no two words are anagrams -> every group has size 1
duplicate words are kept, not de-duplicated
words of differing lengths grouped correctly
testCases.input: a ab abc ba bca cab
testCases.expectedOutput:
a
ab ba
abc bca cab

testCases.description: longer input with multiple groups, a duplicate, and a singleton, exercising group ordering
testCases.input: listen silent enlist eat tea ate cat act dog god listen bat tab tan
testCases.expectedOutput:
act cat
ate eat tea
bat tab
dog god
enlist listen listen silent
tan
